summary: Codebase Atlas helps people understand how software fits together. It reads a local folder, borrows a computer’s scan, or opens a public repository on GitHub, then joins the file facts with a story written by a person or their coding agent. Three screens let you follow what travels between parts, find their files, and look inside them. Atlas checks story references and reports gaps; it never runs the code or writes the story itself.

actors.name: Someone trying to understand a codebase
actors.blurb: A new joiner, a designer, anyone who needs to know how the software fits together.

actors.name: A coding agent
actors.blurb: Uses Atlas’s rules and scan facts to write the story, then checks it. It can also read a scan as JSON to answer questions.

actors.name: The desktop app
actors.blurb: A Mac, Windows or Linux window that asks the local reader to scan a folder and passes the result to the screens.

actors.name: The command line
actors.blurb: Runs atlas scan, atlas serve, and atlas story brief or check. Scripts and coding agents can use it without opening a window.

actors.name: The companion connection
actors.blurb: A phone, iPad or browser pairs with a computer using a code or QR. It receives the scan without copying the repository.

actors.name: The folder reader
actors.blurb: Walks a folder, respects ignored paths, counts lines, and gathers code facts and the checked story into one description.

actors.name: The code parser
actors.blurb: Reads supported code to find declared names and imports. It resolves file links where it can; it does not run the program.

actors.name: The story checker
actors.blurb: Checks story parts, file paths, exchanges and journeys against the file list, locally or in the browser. It reports invalid references; it cannot judge whether the prose is true.

actors.name: The one description
actors.blurb: An in-memory description of the files, code facts, checked story and warnings. Local scans include details that GitHub’s file list cannot supply.

actors.name: The three screens
actors.blurb: How it works follows a journey. Where it lives locates the files; Inside a part shows names and imports. Hairline figures mark the parts.

actors.name: A folder of code
actors.blurb: A repository on a computer’s disk. Atlas reads its files and never runs or changes them.

actors.name: The hand-written story
actors.blurb: The .codebase-index/_story.json file records parts, exchanges and journeys. A person or coding agent writes it; committing it makes it available on GitHub.

actors.name: GitHub
actors.blurb: Supplies a public repository’s file list and, when present, its committed story from the default branch. It does not supply source code or import details.

actors.name: The local scan entrance
actors.blurb: Gives the desktop, command line and sharing server the same way to ask for a local scan.

actors.name: The computer’s sharing door
actors.blurb: The desktop Share session or atlas serve checks the pairing code and limits requests to shared folders.

actors.name: The browser’s GitHub reader
actors.blurb: Checks the repository URL, fetches its file list and optional story, and asks the browser’s story checker to validate the references.

actors.name: The story-writing guide
actors.blurb: Builds atlas story brief from rules and scan facts. atlas story check reports warnings and coverage; shared rules decide which files count as product code.

flows.carries: The person chooses a local folder to explore.
flows.returns: The desktop receives a scan to show in the three screens.

flows.carries: The agent asks to scan a folder, prepare a story brief, or check the story.
flows.returns: The command prints scan JSON, an authoring brief, or warnings and coverage.

flows.carries: The person supplies the computer’s address and pairing code, then chooses a shared folder.
flows.returns: The companion receives that folder’s description for the three screens.

flows.carries: The companion requests a shared folder’s scan with its pairing code.
flows.returns: The computer sends the description or explains why access failed.

flows.carries: The sharing server passes an allowed folder to the local scan entrance.
flows.returns: The scan entrance returns the computer’s description of that folder.

flows.carries: The desktop asks for a scan of the selected folder.
flows.returns: The scan entrance returns the folder’s description and warnings.

flows.carries: The scan command passes the requested folder to the local scan entrance.
flows.returns: The scan entrance returns a description ready to print as JSON.

flows.carries: The local scan entrance asks the folder reader to read this repository.
flows.returns: The folder reader returns file facts, code facts, the checked story and warnings.

flows.carries: The folder reader asks which files are present and reads bounded text where needed.
flows.returns: The folder supplies paths, sizes and text for counting and parsing.

flows.carries: The folder reader passes supported source files to the code parser.
flows.returns: The parser returns declared names and resolved imports where available.

flows.carries: The folder reader asks for the repository’s story to be checked against the scanned files.
flows.returns: The checker returns usable story references and warnings about invalid ones.

flows.carries: The local checker reads the story file beside the repository.
flows.returns: The file supplies the written parts, exchanges and journeys.

flows.carries: The folder reader assembles the scan facts and checked story into one description.
flows.returns: The completed description is available to the caller that requested the scan.

flows.carries: The description supplies file facts, the checked story and warnings to the three screens.
The desktop passes the local description to the three screens.
The companion passes the computer’s description to the three screens.
The person opens a public repository’s URL or explores the selected description.
flows.returns: The screens show the available story and facts, explaining any missing details.

flows.carries: The screens ask the browser’s reader to load the public repository URL.
flows.returns: The reader returns the file list, checked story when available, and warnings.

flows.carries: The browser requests repository details, the file tree and the optional committed story.
flows.returns: GitHub returns the default branch’s file list and story, without source code or imports.

flows.carries: The browser passes the fetched story and file paths to its story checker.
flows.returns: The checker returns usable story references and warnings about invalid ones.

flows.carries: The browser assembles the public file list and checked story into the shared description.
The command runs atlas story brief or atlas story check for the chosen repository.
flows.returns: The guide returns rules, scan facts and the existing story, or validation warnings and product-source coverage.

flows.carries: The guide requests a fresh repository scan before preparing its brief or check report.
flows.returns: The scan entrance returns file facts, the checked story and warnings.

flows.carries: The brief reads the original story file so the agent can inspect and repair it.
flows.returns: The file returns the existing prose, including references that validation rejected.

flows.carries: The coding agent writes or revises the story file using the brief and its understanding of the code.
flows.returns: The saved story is ready for atlas story check to read.

journeys.name: Someone opens a folder on their laptop
journeys.blurb: The local reader gathers code facts and checks the story before the screens show them. Nothing leaves the machine.

journeys.name: Someone opens a public repository on the web
journeys.blurb: GitHub supplies a file list and an optional committed story. The browser checks the story; source code, imports and line counts are unavailable.

journeys.name: An agent writes the story
journeys.blurb: The agent reads atlas story brief, writes the file itself, then runs atlas story check for fresh validation and coverage. Atlas calls no model.

journeys.name: An agent reads the codebase instead of looking at it
journeys.blurb: atlas scan returns the same local description as JSON, with no screen involved.

journeys.name: An iPad borrows a computer’s eyes
journeys.blurb: The pairing code opens access only to shared folders. The computer sends a scan; the tablet shows it without copying the repository.
